title: MedSync clerking examination catalogue
scope: Adult examination for the clerking desk: vital signs and anthropometry, General (appearance, distress, consciousness, attachments, signs, hydration and nutrition), nine systems and a diabetic foot screen. Paediatric, obstetric and gynaecological examination are out of scope.

conventions.ids: Items are "ex.<system>.<item>", snake_case. Attribute and option ids are local to their item. The app stores ids and the catalogue version; labels render at read time.
conventions.companion: Symptom ids (sym.*), past-history condition ids and REF-FLAG-* entries referenced here come from MS-EMR-CLERK-CAT-001 (history catalogue v1).

response_types.presence: A sign that is Absent or Present. Absent is written as "no X". Present opens the attributes.
response_types.test: A manoeuvre that is Negative or Positive.
response_types.state: A structure with an expected state and an unexpected one, with the item's own words (Central/Deviated, Resonant/Abnormal, Intact/Impaired). The only type that uses Normal/Abnormal, and only where a normal state exists.
response_types.device: An attachment that is None or In place. Never normal or abnormal. In place opens the device's properties.
response_types.choice: One of several states; each option is marked expected or not, and may carry its own attributes (oxygen modalities).
response_types.classified: A set of signs that a classifier grades (hydration by GTFCC). The clinician ticks signs; the grade is computed and shown with its reason.
response_types.measured: A measurement that a classifier grades (MUAC by Uganda IMAM).
response_types.link: A read-only view of a fact owned by another item or block, with a link to its owner.
response_types.block: A structured block (consciousness, AMTS, motor grids, pulses grid) specified in scales and classifiers.

attribute_kinds.one: single choice, tap again to clear
attribute_kinds.number: stepper with unit, default, step, min and max
attribute_kinds.zones: a body map (lungs front and back, abdomen nine regions, spine levels)
attribute_kinds.shared: the same fact as another item's attribute, edited in either place

conventions.shown_when: An attribute with shown_when renders only when that attribute holds one of the listed option ids; hiding it clears nothing until the entry is saved without it.
conventions.answer_states: Every item is unrecorded, negative (the expected state), positive, or not examined (with a reason). Unrecorded is never written as negative.
conventions.sensitivity: standard, or a restricted class (hiv, sexual_reproductive_health). Restricted items carry a lock, appear in clinical views only and never in patient-facing text. An option may carry its own restricted class (GATE A, TM2): the option is withheld from patient-facing text wherever it is recorded.
conventions.applies_to_sex: null for everyone; "male" hides the item for other recorded sexes; an unrecorded sex shows the item with a prompt to record sex.
conventions.in_prototype: false marks content added after the prototype: build it from the same response types; there is no screenshot for it.
conventions.statuses: draft, draft-verified-source (an opened source states it), draft-unverified (source not opened or no single source), signed (after GATE A). A flag or classifier whose REF entry is not signed does not fire or show.

GCS-AID.title: Glasgow Coma Scale: Assessment Aid (English), glasgowcomascale.org
GCS-AID.note: Non-testable components are recorded as NT, never scored 1. "None" applies only when nothing interferes.

GCS-P.title: Brennan PM, Murray GD, Teasdale GM. The GCS-Pupils score. J Neurosurg 2018;128(6):1612-20

RCP-NEWS2.title: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2, final report (2017)
RCP-NEWS2.note: Scale 2 is chosen by a competent clinical decision maker for hypercapnic respiratory failure and recorded in the notes.

MRC-45.title: MRC Memorandum No. 45: Aids to the examination of the peripheral nervous system (UKRI)
MRC-45.note: Grades 4-, 4 and 4+ may be used for slight, moderate and strong resistance.

NINDS-REFLEX.title: Physiology, Deep Tendon Reflexes (StatPearls), reproducing the NINDS scale (Hallett, Neurology 1993;43:2723)

PITTING-SCALE.title: Pitting oedema grading (Cleveland Clinic)
PITTING-SCALE.note: No single canonical scale exists; sources differ on rebound times. Sign one scale as house standard.

CLUBBING-GRADES.title: Djojodibroto RD et al. Finger clubbing: do we require digital index quantitator? Med J Malaysia 2014;69(2):60-3 (citing Sarkar, Lung India 2012)

HACKETT.title: Hackett spleen classification, as tabulated in: Hyper-reactive malarial splenomegaly, a systematic review. Malaria Journal 2015 (Table 1)
HACKETT.note: Original: Hackett LW, J Natl Malar Soc 1944. Not a WHO scale.

AMTS-BGS.title: British Geriatrics Society. Abbreviated Mental Test Score (Hodkinson 1972)
AMTS-BGS.note: BGS: 6 or less suggests delirium or dementia. Many UK acute units use 7 or less; CRB-65 uses 8 or less for "confusion".

RASS.title: Sessler CN et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002;166:1338-44

VIP-JACKSON.title: Visual Infusion Phlebitis score (Jackson A, Nurs Times 1998;94(4):68-71), scorecard

WHO-GOITRE.title: WHO/UNICEF/ICCIDD. Assessment of iodine deficiency disorders and monitoring their elimination, 3rd ed. (2007), Table 6

GTFCC-2024.title: GTFCC Cholera patient treatment flowchart v1.0 (9 Sep 2024)
GTFCC-2024.note: Severe: any danger sign, or 2 of sunken eyes, drinks poorly, skin pinch very slow. Some: 2 of restless, sunken eyes, rapid pulse, thirsty, skin pinch slow.

UG-IMAM-2016.title: Ministry of Health Uganda. Guidelines for Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (Jan 2016), Table 2
UG-IMAM-2016.note: Read from the WHO policy repository copy; the MoH library copy would not open. Adult SAM is under 19.0 cm (not 18.5). The NACS manual gives a different pregnant/lactating MAM bound (22 cm); IMAM (23 cm) is used.

WHO-BMI.title: WHO TRS 894. Obesity: preventing and managing the global epidemic (2000), Table 2.1; thinness grades from WHO TRS 854 (1995)

WHO-WAIST-2008.title: WHO. Waist circumference and waist-hip ratio: report of a WHO expert consultation (2008, published 2011)
WHO-WAIST-2008.note: WHO writes "above" 94/80 and 102/88; IDF writes "at least".

IDF-2006.title: IDF consensus worldwide definition of the metabolic syndrome (2006), Table 2
IDF-2006.note: Sub-Saharan Africans: use European cut-offs until more specific data are available.

NICE-NG246.title: NICE NG246 Overweight and obesity management (2025)
NICE-NG246.note: Waist-to-height ratio 0.5-0.59 increased risk; 0.6 or more high.

SIGN-158.title: BTS/SIGN British guideline on the management of asthma (SIGN 158, 2019), acute asthma in adults, retained in the BTS/NICE/SIGN asthma pathway (SIGN 244, 2024)

OH-CONSENSUS-2011.title: Freeman R et al. Consensus statement on the definition of orthostatic hypotension. Clin Auton Res 2011;21:69-72

NICE-NG136.title: NICE NG136 Hypertension in adults, recommendation 1.2.1 (updated Feb 2026)

ADA-SOC-2025.title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2025, section 6, Table 6.4 (hypoglycaemia levels)
ADA-SOC-2025.note: The 2026 section was renamed; its summary of revisions shows no change to the levels. Confirm at Phase 0.

HYPERGLYCAEMIC-CRISIS.title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, section 16, Table 16.1: DKA and HHS criteria (glucose 11.1 mmol/L with ketones)
HYPERGLYCAEMIC-CRISIS.note: About 10% of DKA presents with glucose below 11.1 mmol/L (euglycaemic DKA).

NICE-NG250.title: NICE NG250 Pneumonia: diagnosis and management (Sep 2025), recommendation 1.2.2 (CRB65)

SSC-2026.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines 2026 (Intensive Care Med 2026;52:863-936), recommendation 4
SSC-2026.note: Use NEWS, NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS over qSOFA as a single screening tool. Hence no qSOFA here.

UCG-2023.title: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023, Ministry of Health
UCG-2023.note: Section 1.1.6 (p. 24-25): symptoms generally occur below 3.0 mmol/L. No equivalent of ADA level 1.

IWGDF-2023.title: IWGDF 2023 Practical guidelines on the prevention and management of diabetes-related foot disease
IWGDF-2023.note: Monofilament: three sites per foot from Figure 4 (not named in text); 2 of 3 correct = felt. Ipswich touch test when no monofilament or fork.

IWGDF-IDSA-2023.title: IWGDF/IDSA 2023 guidelines on diabetes-related foot infections (classification table)

IWGDF-SINBAD.title: IWGDF 2023 guidelines on the classification of foot ulcers (SINBAD, recommendation 1a)

ITT.title: Rayman G et al. The Ipswich Touch Test. Diabetes Care 2011;34:1517-8
ITT.note: Tips of toes 1, 3 and 5 on both feet; 2 or more of 6 not felt = at risk (Rayman 2011). The count spans both feet.

WHO-HIV-STAGING.title: WHO clinical staging of HIV disease in adults, adolescents and children (Consolidated ARV guidelines 2016, annex)

BTS-O2-2017.title: BTS guideline for oxygen use in adults in healthcare and emergency settings (Thorax 2017)
BTS-O2-2017.note: Targets 94-98% and 88-92%; reservoir mask 15 L/min. A new BTS target-saturation guideline is due in 2026: check at Phase 0.

AASLD-HE-2014.title: Vilstrup H et al. Hepatic encephalopathy in chronic liver disease: AASLD/EASL practice guideline 2014, Table 2 (West Haven)

GIRFT-CES-2026.title: GIRFT National suspected cauda equina syndrome pathway (March 2026)
GIRFT-CES-2026.note: Emergency MRI as soon as possible and within 4 hours of request.

NICE-NG240.title: NICE NG240 Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease (2024)

NICE-NG240-EV.title: NICE NG240 evidence review: symptoms and signs of bacterial meningitis

UMDPC-ETHICS.title: Uganda Medical and Dental Practitioners Council. Code of Professional Ethics (2013 reprint)
UMDPC-ETHICS.note: Has consent, privacy and decency duties but no chaperone provision. The chaperone rule rests on these plus the GMC guidance.

NICE-NG128.title: NICE NG128 Stroke and TIA in over 16s (2022), recommendations 1.1.1-1.1.3
NICE-NG128.note: FAST outside hospital; a validated tool such as ROSIER in the emergency department; exclude hypoglycaemia first.

ROSIER.title: Nor AM et al. The ROSIER scale. Lancet Neurol 2005;4:727-34
ROSIER.note: Weights, the >0 cut-off and the <3.5 mmol/L pre-check checked against the NHS form (the Lancet full text was not accessible). The +1 signs count only when new.

CLINICAL-METHODS.title: Walker HK, Hall WD, Hurst JW. Clinical Methods, 3rd ed. (NCBI Bookshelf)

OPERATIONAL.title: MedSync operational rule (no external source; CSO decision)

DRAFT-MEDSYNC.title: MedSync draft clinical rule, awaiting CSO sign-off (no single external source)

WHO-EVD-CASEDEF.title: WHO. Case definition recommendations for Ebola or Marburg virus diseases, interim guideline WHO/EVD/CaseDef/14.1 (9 Aug 2014)
WHO-EVD-CASEDEF.note: Says "fever" with no number. The 38.0 °C threshold is an operational CSO value (SC5).

UG-IDSR-2021.title: MoH Uganda. National Technical Guidelines for IDSR, 3rd edition (Sep 2021): acute haemorrhagic fever syndrome, Ebola or Marburg
UG-IDSR-2021.note: During an outbreak, unexplained bleeding alone is a suspected case.

NICE-CG95.title: NICE CG95. Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin (2010, updated 2016), recommendations 1.2.2.8 and 1.2.4.2

WHO-MALARIA.title: WHO guidelines for malaria (13 Aug 2025); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 §2.5.2 (complete physical examination in any patient with fever)

WHO-TB-SCREEN-2021.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 2: screening (2021), §3.1
WHO-TB-SCREEN-2021.note: Lists haemoptysis as a TB symptom; no examination content. UCG 2023 §5.3.1 supports the node, clubbing and MUAC suggestions.

ADA-EASD-CRISES-2024.title: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report (Umpierrez GE et al.; ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS). Diabetes Care 2024;47(8):1257-1275; Diabetologia 2024;67:1455-1479

TREND-UK-2020.title: Type 1 diabetes: what to do when you are ill (TREND-UK leaflet)

ICO-2017.title: Guidelines on Diabetic Eye Care: The International Council of Ophthalmology Recommendations for Screening, Follow-up, Referral, and Treatment Based on Resource Settings (Wong TY et al., Ophthalmology 2018;125:1608-1622; doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2018.04.007)

EADSG-2019.title: EADSG Guidelines: Insulin Storage and Optimisation of Injection Technique in Diabetes Management
EADSG-2019.edition: East Africa Diabetes Study Group 2019 (Bahendeka S, et al. Diabetes Ther 2019;10(2):341–366)

WHO-PEN-TRAINING.title: Training manual: WHO Package of Essential NCD Interventions (PEN) - Management of type 2 diabetes
WHO-PEN-TRAINING.edition: WHO PEN training manual (undated; mirrors HEARTS-D 2020, WHO/UCN/NCD/20.1)

WHO-HEARTS-D-2020.title: Diagnosis and management of type 2 diabetes (HEARTS-D)

ADA-SOC-2026.title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026

ICDR-2003.title: Proposed International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema Disease Severity Scales (Wilkinson CP et al., Ophthalmology 2003;110:1677-1682)

REF-EX-GCS-AIRWAY.meaning: At or below this, protect the airway

REF-EX-GTFCC-COUNT.meaning: Signs needed within a GTFCC group

REF-EX-MUAC-BANDS.meaning: Uganda IMAM MUAC bands from age 15. Bilateral pitting oedema is SAM only once non-nutritional causes are excluded by the clinician

REF-EX-BMI-BANDS.meaning: Upper bounds (exclusive) of the WHO adult BMI classes, age 20 and over

REF-EX-BMI-ADULT-AGE.meaning: Adult BMI classes apply from this age; younger patients need BMI-for-age (out of scope)

REF-EX-WAIST.meaning: Waist risk thresholds (at or above; IDF uses at or above, WHO "above": sign one)

REF-EX-OH-SBP.meaning: Sustained systolic fall within 3 min of standing

REF-EX-OH-DBP.meaning: Sustained diastolic fall within 3 min of standing

REF-EX-ARM-DIFF.meaning: Systolic difference between arms: repeat, then use the higher arm

REF-EX-GLU-HIGH.meaning: At or above this: check ketones (hyperglycaemic crisis criteria)

REF-EX-ASTHMA-RR.meaning: Acute severe asthma: respiratory rate at or above

REF-EX-ASTHMA-HR.meaning: Acute severe asthma: heart rate at or above

REF-EX-AMTS-IMPAIRED.meaning: At or below this suggests delirium or dementia (BGS). Prototype used 7: CSO to choose

REF-EX-VIP-RESITE.meaning: At or above this, resite the cannula

REF-EX-POWER-WEAK.meaning: At or below this in any muscle group: marked weakness

REF-EX-NRS-BANDS.meaning: Pain severity bands on the numerical rating scale

REF-EX-ITT-LOPS.meaning: Ipswich touch test: this many or more not felt means loss of protective sensation

REF-EX-SINBAD-AREA.meaning: SINBAD area point at or above

REF-EX-CRT.meaning: Capillary refill longer than this is delayed

REF-EX-BP-SEVERE.meaning: Severe hypertension: same-day assessment if retinal haemorrhage, papilloedema or life-threatening symptoms

REF-EX-SBP-LOW.meaning: Systolic below this with poor perfusion signs: shock

REF-EX-FEVER-TEMP.meaning: Fever threshold for the fever-with-bleeding flag. An operational CSO value: the WHO and Uganda IDSR case definitions say "fever" with no number; Uganda VHF surveillance uses > 38 °C.

REF-EX-OLDER-AGE.meaning: Age from which AMTS, lying and standing BP and pressure areas are suggested

REF-EX-PROSTATE-AGE.meaning: Age from which a prostate examination is suggested with back pain in a man

REF-EX-SPO2-SCORE-SUGGEST.meaning: At or above this, suggest the respiratory examination

REF-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST.meaning: WHO primary care: measure urine ketones when plasma glucose is at or above this value

REF-EX-KETONE-DKA.meaning: DKA: blood beta-hydroxybutyrate at or above this value

REF-EX-KETONE-RISK.meaning: Blood ketones at or above this value (and below 3.0): at risk of DKA, contact the diabetes team as soon as possible

REF-EX-KETONE-RAISED.meaning: Blood ketones at or above this value are raised

REF-EX-DR-RECALL.meaning: Re-examination interval by grade. Mild and moderate use the near end of ICO's range; the far end applies only where control is confirmed at target.

gcs.label: Glasgow Coma Scale

E: Eyes closed by swelling or dressing

rules: A component that cannot be tested is recorded as NT with its reason, never as 1.
The total is shown only when all three components are scored.
The note writes the total with its parts: "GCS 13/15 (E3 V4 M6)". With NT: "GCS not totalled (E3 VNT M6)".

acvpu.label: ACVPU (NEWS2)
acvpu.news2: A scores 0; C, V, P and U score 3.

pupil_reactivity.label: Pupil reactivity score (for GCS-P)
pupil_reactivity.rule: Both unreactive = 2; one unreactive = 1; both react (brisk or sluggish) = 0. GCS-P = GCS total minus the score (range 1-15).

ninds_reflex.label: NINDS reflex scale
grades: Enhanced, more than normal (includes clonus if present)

levine.label: Levine murmur grade
grades: Heard with the stethoscope lightly on the chest
Heard with the stethoscope off the chest

npiap.label: NPIAP pressure injury stage
npiap.note: Device-related injuries are staged; mucosal injuries are not.

amts.label: Abbreviated Mental Test Score

items.text: Address given for recall (e.g. Plot 42, Kampala Road)
Name of the current President of Uganda

amts.note: Items 3, 8 and 9 are adapted for Uganda (address, year of independence 1962, current President). The adapted wording needs CSO sign-off and local validation; results are advisory.

west_haven.label: West Haven hepatic encephalopathy grade
grades: Oriented; subtle change in behaviour or attention
Disoriented to place; somnolent but rousable
west_haven.rule: Chosen by the clinician. The app suggests a grade from orientation and GCS but never sets it.

dehydration_gtfcc.label: Dehydration (GTFCC)
dehydration_gtfcc.not_applicable: Signs are recorded but not graded: "The GTFCC table grades dehydration from diarrhoea or vomiting."
dehydration_gtfcc.counting: Each severe-column sign also counts toward "some" (very slow pinch implies slow; drinks poorly counts in the thirst column). Sunken eyes counts once per group. Slow and very slow pinch together count once.

below_threshold.label: Signs below the GTFCC threshold: reassess

hint_suppressed_when.show_instead: Fluid overload signs present: plan the fluids with care

dehydration_gtfcc.display: Result pill with its reason ("danger sign: lethargic"). The treatment hint is shown, never written to the plan.

muac_uganda_imam.label: Acute malnutrition by MUAC (Uganda IMAM)
muac_uganda_imam.band_from: patient age; pregnant_or_lactating qualifier for female patients

oedema_rule.result: sam only when oedema_cause is nutritional; otherwise "Bilateral pitting oedema: exclude heart, kidney, liver and pregnancy causes"
oedema_rule.why: Uganda IMAM 2016: in adults, oedema must be interpreted with caution and medical causes ruled out.

muac_uganda_imam.note: Children under 15 use different MUAC cut-offs and weight-for-height (out of scope; the classifier returns "not applicable" under 15).

bmi_who.label: BMI class (WHO)
bmi_who.not_applicable: Pregnancy, or age under the adult threshold: shows "BMI class not applicable".

waist_risk.label: Waist circumference risk
waist_risk.note: Prototype assumed a male patient; the build reads sex from the record and shows "Record sex to classify" when it is missing.

respiratory_distress_severity.label: Respiratory distress severity
respiratory_distress_severity.note: No single validated adult score exists for general respiratory distress. This grading is a MedSync draft built from the SIGN 158 severity features (words only, exhaustion) and the WHO/ETAT signs (grunting, recession). Where asthma is the context, acute_asthma_severity takes precedence in the note. CSO to sign or replace.

distress_severity.label: Distress severity
distress_severity.rule: The overall grade is the highest component grade. Each component shows its own grade and inputs. Respiratory signs are the shared fact owned by Respiratory, work of breathing.

gcs_total.label: GCS total
gcs_total.rule: E + V + M when all three are scored; null when any is NT or missing.

gcs_p.label: GCS-Pupils
gcs_p.rule: gcs_total minus the pupil reactivity score (scales.pupil_reactivity). Computed whenever GCS and both pupil reactions are recorded; written to the note and shown in the block only when the pupil score is above 0.

acvpu_from_consciousness.label: ACVPU for NEWS2
rules: GCS 15 gives A.

GCS below 15 does not map by itself: the clinician chooses C, V, P or U, with a suggestion: V4 or V5 with eyes open suggests C if the confusion is new; M6 or any verbal response suggests at least V; any motor response to pressure (M2-M5) with no response to voice suggests P; only E1 V1 M1 suggests U.
Where ACVPU is chosen directly, it is used as is.
Until a level exists, the vitals rail says "choose ACVPU in General" and NEWS2 is incomplete, never scored as A.

orientation.label: Orientation
rules: V5 (orientated) means oriented to person, place and time: orientation is derived and shown read-only.
V4 (confused): ask time, place and person, each yes or no.
V3 or below, or V not testable: "orientation not assessable".
With ACVPU A, orientation is asked directly (time, place, person).

inter_arm_difference.label: BP difference between arms
inter_arm_difference.rule: Systolic difference above REF-EX-ARM-DIFF: "repeat"; if still above on repeat, later readings use the higher arm (the vitals BP defaults its arm).

acute_asthma_severity.label: Acute asthma severity (adults)

applies_when.panel_confirm: The clinician confirms "acute asthma" in the panel. The panel is offered when there is wheeze, sym.wheeze or known asthma or COPD.

acute_asthma_severity.suppressed_when: SpO2 scale 2 or an oxygen target of 88-92% is recorded (COPD or hypercapnic risk): the panel says "Asthma severity not applied: hypercapnic target recorded".
acute_asthma_severity.note: Arrhythmia, hypotension and blood-gas criteria are clinician judgements or laboratory data and are not inferred. "Cannot complete sentences" maps to "speaks in words only".

crb65.label: CRB65
points: confusion: AMTS at or below 8, or new disorientation in person, place or time
systolic below 90 or diastolic at or below 60
crb65.display: Shown in the Respiratory card with each point ticked or not; written to the note with its points.

hypoglycaemia_level.label: Hypoglycaemia level
hypoglycaemia_level.note: Level 2 (below 3.0 mmol/L) matches UCG 2023 §1.1.6 for everyone. Level 1 (3.0 to 3.8) is urgent only in a patient with diabetes (history or glucose-lowering medicine), caution otherwise (GATE A, SC1).

rosier.label: ROSIER
rosier.pre_check: Glucose must be recorded first; below 3.5 mmol/L treat and reassess (ROSIER). The score is hidden until glucose is recorded.

results.unlikely: 0 or below: stroke unlikely, not excluded

rosier.note: The history items (syncope, seizure) must be from this episode; the clinician confirms them in the ROSIER panel. Each +1 sign scores only when the clinician confirms in the panel that it is new since the symptoms began (GATE A, SC3).

iwgdf_risk.label: IWGDF foot risk category
iwgdf_risk.per: foot, then the higher of the two

derived.lops: monofilament not felt at a site on that foot, or vibration not felt on that side, or an Ipswich touch test at or above REF-EX-ITT-LOPS (the test counts both feet, so it marks loss of protective sensation on both)
derived.pad: dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial pulse absent on that side (pulses grid)
derived.deformity: foot deformity present on that side
derived.high_risk_history: previous foot ulcer, amputation (history or deformity options), or end-stage kidney disease

rules.when: lops and pad; or lops and deformity; or pad and deformity

results.0: Very low risk: screen once a year

iwgdf_risk.requires: Both feet screened for sensation and pulses; otherwise "incomplete".
iwgdf_risk.note: IWGDF risk stratification is for people without an active ulcer. With an active ulcer the panel shows the category with "active ulcer: manage the ulcer; the screening interval applies after healing". A current ulcer is not "history of ulcer".

dfi_iwgdf_idsa.label: Diabetic foot infection (IWGDF/IDSA)

rules.when: local infection (2 or more local signs) plus 2 or more SIRS signs from the draft vitals (temperature above 38 or below 36 °C, pulse above 90, respiratory rate above 20)
local infection (2 or more local signs) and either redness 2 cm or more from the edge, or involvement deeper than skin and subcutaneous tissue
2 or more of: swelling or induration, redness 0.5 to under 2 cm, local tenderness, local warmth, pus

dfi_iwgdf_idsa.suffix: (O) after grade 3 or 4 when the clinician records osteomyelitis as suspected or confirmed. Probes to bone offers "(O) suggested" for the clinician to confirm.
dfi_iwgdf_idsa.note: The white cell count is not in the examination; the clinician can upgrade to severe from laboratory data.

sinbad.label: SINBAD
points: Ischaemia: no palpable pedal pulse on that side (dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial both absent); one palpable pulse scores 0
Bacterial infection: IWGDF/IDSA grade 2 or more
sinbad.rule: Total 0-6. The note states each component present or absent, as IWGDF recommends, not the total alone.

umn_lmn_pattern.label: Motor pattern hint
umn_lmn_pattern.rule: Upper: increased tone (spastic), reflexes grade 4 or clonus, extensor plantar, Hoffmann positive (grade 3 is the upper half of normal and does not count). Lower: wasting, fasciculation, reduced tone, reflexes 0-1. Mixed shows both.
umn_lmn_pattern.note: A hint beside the motor grids only. Never written to the note: the note records findings, not interpretations.

news2.label: NEWS2
news2.rule: Reused from the triage engine; inputs from the draft vital-signs set, ACVPU and air or oxygen.

acuity_band.label: Visual acuity
acuity_band.note: Either eye. ICO refers when acuity is worse than 6/12 whatever the retinal grade; the line is the dossier's REF-DM-EYE-REFER-VA.

ketone_band.label: Ketones
ketone_band.note: First match wins. The bands are named as findings (high, moderate, raised), not as diagnoses: a fasting or vomiting person without diabetes can have high ketones. Urine strips lag behind blood ketones: a low strip with a ketoacidotic picture is not reassurance. The urine cut (2+) is the dossier's REF-DM-ACU-DKA-UKET.

dr_review.label: Retinopathy: next step

rules.text: Refer to an ophthalmologist within 1 month
Refer to an ophthalmologist within 3 months
Refer: the retina or vision cannot be assessed here
Refer routinely, and re-examine in 3 months
Re-examine at the interval for this grade
Incomplete: needs a dilated or photographic view and the acuity

dr_review.note: First match wins, most urgent first. ICO: refer when acuity is worse than 6/12 or there are visual symptoms, whatever the grade, and when the retina cannot be seen. 're_examine_by_grade' needs an adequate dilated or photographic view AND a recorded acuity; without them the result is 'incomplete', never a reassuring interval. Uganda's Eye Care Guidelines 2016 refer everyone with diabetes to a retina clinic: the CSO chooses between that rule and ICO's (D-DM-14). The acuity classifier is new.
dr_review.reconcile: sym.blurred_vision id; the 'recorded' atom on an item

vital_signs.principle: Vital signs are written through the existing observation action as a new set; the examination never copies a set. The triage set stays read-only beside the new draft.

fields.label: Pulse
fields.rule: An irregular rhythm asks for an apical count over 60 seconds and shows the apex-radial deficit.

fields.label: SpO₂
fields.rule: Scale 2 only when a clinician has recorded hypercapnic respiratory failure with a target of 88-92% (RCP-NEWS2). Air or oxygen comes from General, attachments.

fields.label: Capillary glucose
fields.rule: One field with a required context; mg/dL entry converts by 18.0 and stores mmol/L. A meter reading above or below its range is recorded as HI or LO, never as a number (EC-6).

composer.principle: The examination paragraph is assembled from structured findings by fixed rules (no AI). The clinician edits it before signing; an edited block stops regenerating.
rules: Order: vital signs line, then General, then systems in catalogue order, then Feet. Within a system, parts in catalogue order (inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation).

Vital signs: "BP 118/76 (right arm, sitting), pulse 58 regular, RR 14, SpO₂ 96% on room air, temperature 35.8 °C (axillary), glucose 6.1 mmol/L (random). NEWS2 1." Missing parameters are listed: "Not measured: weight."
Anthropometry: "Weight 61 kg, height 170 cm, BMI 21.1 (normal weight). Waist 84 cm (low risk), waist-to-height 0.49. MUAC 24 cm."
Consciousness: "GCS 13/15 (E3 V4 M6), not oriented to time" or "ACVPU: new confusion"; "(known baseline)" when so marked. GCS-P is added only when the pupil score is above 0.

Positive findings first in each system, each with its attributes as a clause in catalogue order; then negatives joined with "; ". Example: "Crackles, fine, late inspiratory, in the right and left lower zones (back). Trachea central; expansion symmetrical; percussion resonant."

Presence items write their phrase.negative ("no clubbing"); state items their phrase.negative ("apex beat normal"); device items write only when in place ("peripheral cannula 20 G, left forearm, day 2, VIP 0").
Choice items write the chosen option ("propped up, cannot lie flat"); an expected choice writes as a negative ("lying comfortably").

Classified items write the result with its inputs: "Some dehydration (GTFCC: sunken eyes, drinks eagerly)". Outside the classifier's scope they write the signs only ("sunken eyes, dry mucosa"). Treatment hints are never written.

Scores write with their parts: "Power: right hip flexion 3/5, left 5/5"; "Reflexes: knee R 3, L 2"; "Murmur: pansystolic, grade 3/6, loudest at the apex, radiating to the axilla"; "SINBAD 3 (site forefoot 0, ischaemia 1, neuropathy 1, infection 0, area 1, depth 0)".
Linked items are written once, by their owner. The reader's paragraph does not repeat them.
Mirrored options (for example oral thrush shown under HIV-associated signs) are written once, by the owner item; the HIV paragraph lists only its own options.
Not examined: "Not examined: rectal (patient declined); fundi (no ophthalmoscope)." Unrecorded items and systems are simply absent; nothing is inferred as normal.
"Everything else normal" writes the negatives of the items it set, not a blanket "normal examination".
Intimate gate: "Chaperone: {name}, {role}. Verbal consent." precedes the rectal and genital paragraph.
Restricted items (hiv, sexual_reproductive_health) appear in the clinical note only; the patient-facing summary excludes them (D-EMR-13).
Hints and display-only classifiers (motor pattern, WHO stage hints, treatment plans) are never written.
Numbers are digits with units and a space before the unit (except % and °); options are lower-cased mid-sentence except proper nouns, abbreviations and eponyms.

prototype_parity.change: Sign "Absent or weak radial pulse" is now "Absent or weak pulse", as worded in the GTFCC cholera patient treatment flowchart (2024).

Grades reworded to the published five-grade description (grade 2 is an increased hyponychial angle; grade 5 is a shiny, glossy change, not hypertrophic osteoarthropathy). Osteoarthropathy is recorded as its own option under "Also".
Grade 3+ rebound reads "15–60 s" (was "within 60 s"). No single canonical pitting scale exists; the catalogue cites one source and marks it for sign-off.
VIP options now carry the scale's action ("resite") so the note and the flag use the source wording.
NPIAP unstageable and deep tissue injury added; device-related injury and mucosal sites added (mucosal injuries are not staged).
"Right/left sluggish or fixed" replaced by a reaction per side (brisk, sluggish, unreactive). GCS-P counts unreactive pupils only.
Venturi 50% added. Valve colours are the manufacturer's and can vary by brand; the percentage is the recorded value.
Psoas, obturator and percussion tenderness added beside guarding, rigidity, rebound, Murphy's and Rovsing's.
High-riding testis and absent cremasteric reflex added (torsion features).
Negative label "Under 2 s" becomes "2 s or less" so exactly 2 s has an answer; delayed is above REF-EX-CRT.
Tongue bite added (suggested after fits).
Stepper start values are no longer stored. The prototype wrote the start value (MUAC 24, monofilament 1, JVP 4 ...) as soon as a finding was positive; a measurement is now stored only once touched.
New item (Higher functions): confrontation fields and neglect, needed by the ROSIER score. Cranial nerve II keeps acuity, RAPD and fundal findings.

New system (not in the prototype): the IWGDF 2023 foot screen (ulcer with SINBAD fields, infection signs, gangrene, deformity, skin, temperature, pulses link, monofilament, 128 Hz fork, Ipswich touch test, risk history) with the IWGDF risk, IWGDF/IDSA infection and SINBAD classifiers.
New item: Characteristic facies.
New item: Bleeding signs (gums, venepuncture sites, conjunctivae ...), which feed the fever-with-bleeding VHF flag.
New item: HIV-associated signs (restricted class hiv), with WHO clinical stage hints that never stage the patient.
New item: Stigmata of chronic liver disease, with a clinician-chosen West Haven grade when asterixis is present.
New item: Hoffmann's sign (no flag on its own: positive in up to 3% of healthy people).

MUAC bands follow the Uganda IMAM guideline by age band (adult SAM under 19.0 cm, MAM 19.0 to under 22.0 cm; 60 and over SAM under 16.0 cm; adolescents 15-17 SAM under 18.5 cm; pregnant or lactating MAM under 23.0 cm). The prototype used 18.5 cm for all adults. A pregnant-or-lactating qualifier is added for female patients. In adults, bilateral pitting oedema makes SAM only when the clinician records it as nutritional (other causes excluded), as IMAM advises.

GTFCC grading now applies only with diarrhoea or vomiting in the history, counts severe-column signs toward "some", and returns "below threshold" rather than "no dehydration" when some signs are ticked. The prototype graded any patient, so pneumonia or heart failure with respiratory distress read "severe dehydration, plan C".

Levels raised to urgent: melaena, reduced GCS (unless marked known baseline), hot swollen joint, severe pallor, level 1 hypoglycaemia, painful retention. Absent foot pulses alone are caution. Power 3 or less is urgent only with new weakness in the history. New urgent flags: fever with bleeding, severe hypertension with organ signs, shock, tamponade, Kussmaul breathing with high glucose.
Badges name the finding, value or standard scale: "Deviated trachea, hyper-resonant chest" (was "Possible tension pneumothorax"), "GTFCC: severe dehydration", "MUAC 17.5 cm", "VIP 2".
The prototype mapped any GCS below 15 with an ACVPU pick; the suggestion rules are corrected (motor response to pressure suggests P; only E1 V1 M1 suggests U).
